issues.location: Running Tests section — exit code bullet
issues.issue: Wiki says 'exit 0 on success, 1 on failure' but the source states three cases: 0 (all pass), 1 (any fail), and 'any other number if an internal error occurs.' Omitting the internal-error exit code is a factual simplification that could mislead a student into treating any non-zero code as a test failure.

The source explicitly warns: 'avoid space and other special characters which might require escaping in shell; also avoid dash (`-`) as a first character of the name, as it could then be interpreted as a command line option and not as a test name.' The wiki omits this entirely. A student naming a test '-something' would hit a real, non-obvious failure that the wiki's Running Tests section wouldn't explain.

issues.location: Assertion Macros table — TEST_ASSERT row and the 'Why TEST_ASSERT's dire consequences are acceptable' paragraph
issues.issue: The source explains the abort mechanism differs by execution mode: 'abort()' when run as a child process, 'longjmp()' when not. The wiki mentions consequences (unflushed FDs, memory leaks) but not the mechanism. The distinction matters because longjmp-based cleanup differs from abort in edge cases — a student reading only the wiki wouldn't know why the same test behaves differently with vs without child-process isolation.

Wiki claims TEST_CHECK 'Logs the failure (with file:line)' but the source never describes the output format or mentions file:line information. This may be accurate based on actual behavior, but it's not verifiable from the provided source.
